messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — Sable (dedicated VPC) reports auth failures for inference endpoints. Impact: multiple 401/502s from customer traffic. Automated ticket INC-9812 created.
Jordan (oncall): I have the page. Assigning to Devon for first triage. Can somebody confirm customer impact (token failures vs proxy errors)?
Devon: seeing 401 spikes then 502s from auth-proxy. Dumping tail of proxy logs:
```
  2026-03-14T09:12:02Z auth-proxy[sable] ERROR fetch_jwks: jwks_fetch 503 from https://idp.sable-corp.com/.well-known/jwks.json
  2026-03-14T09:12:03Z auth-proxy[sable] WARN token_validation failed: no key found for kid=ab12cd
  2026-03-14T09:12:04Z gateway[sable] ERROR upstream: 502 bad gateway -> auth-proxy
  2026-03-14T09:12:05Z auth-proxy[sable] ERROR jwks_rate_limited: status=429
```
Devon: looks like our auth-proxy can't fetch the rotated JWKS; IdP returning 429/503. Token validation falls back to reject -> 401s.
Emily: I chatted with Sable's infra contact (Oliver) — they rotated keys ~08:50 UTC and their IdP is now throttling external JWKS fetches while it stabilizes. They also deployed an internal edge change that briefly returned 503s.
Oliver (acct): yep, we rotated, but the management plane is throttling external clients; we can remove rate-limits but need a short time to confirm no misuse. We're coordinating with their IdP team now.
Jordan (oncall): Customer impact = blocked inference for some users. Priority P1. We need a short-term mitigation that doesn't break tenant isolation. Options: 1) Serve cached JWKS from our side (static), 2) Bypass auth-proxy for Sable's dedicated pool (temp ACL), 3) Ask customer to re-enable previous key for a short TTL. Thoughts?
Maya (eng-runtime): we can serve a cached jwks bundle from internal S3 and hit cache for 30m while IdP heals. Requires uploading a jwks.json and a small flag flip in auth-proxy config. Low risk.
Ana (platform-ops): bypassing auth entirely is risky but we could route Sable's traffic to a dedicated pool with an enforced header check (X-SABLE-OK) set by our ingress that only we can inject — effectively short-circuiting OIDC check while preserving tenant isolation. More invasive and emergency-only.
Lee (sec-ops): bypassing OIDC validation is last resort. Serving cached JWKS is acceptable if we ensure we only use keys we have verifiably seen before (no acceptance of unknown kids). Also add tighter telemetry to audit token acceptance.
Devon: I'll try the cached-JWKS path first. Plan: fetch last known good jwks from our cache, push to internal s3://auth-proxy-cache/sable/jwks.json, flip auth-proxy config: jwks_fallback_s3 = true for tenant sable, restart auth-proxy worker (rolling). Expected window ~3-7 min.
Jordan (oncall): go for it. Notify when done.
Devon: doing now — uploading file and applying config. Command I ran:
```
redwoodctl secrets put s3://auth-proxy-cache/sable/jwks.json --file ./jwks_last_good.json
redwoodctl config set tenant.sable.auth-proxy.jwks_fallback_s3 true
redwoodctl svc restart auth-proxy --tenant sable --rolling
```
Devon: restart in progress, watching logs.
Maya (eng-runtime): watch for KV-cache invalidation in runtime; if tokens have longer TTLs we might still allow valid sessions. Also bump gateway timeout to avoid cascades.
Devon: restart completed. Tail logs now show JWKS load from s3 and token validations succeeding:
```
  2026-03-14T09:18:33Z auth-proxy[sable] INFO jwks_loaded source=s3://auth-proxy-cache/sable/jwks.json
  2026-03-14T09:18:34Z auth-proxy[sable] INFO token_validation success kid=ab12cd
  2026-03-14T09:18:35Z gateway[sable] INFO request proxied to runtime (200)
```
Jordan (oncall): Confirmed: traffic rates back to normal and 401s down. Customer reports partial recovery. :thumbsup:
Oliver (acct): seeing requests succeed now. We'll keep our IdP team working on rate-limits and will coordinate a safer rotation strategy. Thanks.
Emily: I'm creating an incident incident/sable-auth-20260314 for follow-up: action items — permanent JWKS caching policy for dedicated VPCs, pre-warming IdP, support docs for key rotations.
Lee (sec-ops): Postmortem notes: require an allowed-sources list for JWKS fetch to help IdPs whitelist our fetchers or provide a push-based key propagation option (webhook).
Ana (platform-ops): Follow-up infrastructure item: add a flag to allow short-lived per-tenant static jwks to be served automatically after rotation detection for up to X minutes. Need an RFC.
Maya (eng-runtime): Quick config suggestion to avoid similar incidents: increase auth-proxy jwks_cache_ttl from 60s -> 300s for dedicated tenants and add exponential backoff with jitter when fetching.
Devon: capturing commands used and timeline in the ticket.
Jordan (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m — leaving this to Emily and Maya for cleanup/monitoring. If it degrades again, page the oncall rotation.
Emily: I'll monitor dashboards for 2 hours and handle postmortem. Assigning follow-ups: Maya - runtime config change; Ana - RFC; Lee - security checklist; Oliver/Sable - IdP rate-limit agreement.
incident-bot: Incident INC-9812 status updated -> mitigated (temporary cached-JWKS fallback applied).
Jordan (oncall): Thanks team. Closing the live thread — please add any additional notes to the incident ticket.
